title: add-invoke-slice-sampler-and-token-cascade-explainer
author: Samir Patel
description: Motivation: long-tail token cost and latency noise make it hard to correlate bursts to kernel warmup, prefix vs completion cost, and scheduling contention. This PR introduces two complementary observability primitives: (1) an Invoke Slice Sampler that slices invocations into time-aligned 'slices' to preserve bursty token-attribution while dramatically reducing cardinality and storage cost; and (2) a Token Cascade Explainer that attributes per-token cost/latency to a small set of causal contributors (prefix KV hits/misses, kernel warmup penalty, batching wait, and I/O stalls) and exposes an explainer panel in the console. Summary of changes: - New sampler: telemetry/ingest/slice_sampler.go adds a deterministic slice keyed by (tenant, route, invocation_bucket) and emits sampled span anchors plus compact slice digests. Sampler is opt-in via telemetry.config.slice_sampling.enabled=false|true. - Token cascade: pkg/observability/token_cascade.go implements cascade attribution heuristics that correlate per-token timing with kernel occupancy metadata and KV cache events; exposes cascade tags on spans (cascade.stage and cascade.score). - Dashboards: dashboards/invocation_cascade_explainer.json adds a new panel with per-slice token waterfall, kernel warmup heatmap, and slice-level cost breakdown (prefix vs completion vs kernel). - Ingest/transform: telemetry/transform/slice_hydrator.go and telemetry/transform/cascade_enricher.go perform lightweight join of sampled anchors to full spans to produce rollups. - Docs & examples: docs/observability/token-cascade.md and examples/observability/quickstart-slice.sh. - Tests: tests/e2e/observability/synthetic_slice_test.py adds deterministic workload that reproduces warmup-burst patterns and validates attribution. Design notes and rollout: the slice sampler reduces telemetry volume by ~12x on our internal bursty trace workloads; we configured a conservative default sampling rate of 1/100 slices per tenant but added adaptive rate increases for tenants with high SLO sensitivity. The cascade explainer is purely additive instrumentation and will appear as optional panels; it does not change any runtime decision logic. Backwards compatibility: existing span shapes and tags remain unchanged unless telemetry.config.cascade_enrichment.enabled=true. Rollout plan: feature flag gated, staged rollout over 2 weeks: opt-in in staging, 10% of production tenants, 50% after stability checks, full rollout. Testing: unit tests for sampler determinism, integration tests for hydration path, and e2e synthetic replay. Checklist: - [x] implement sampler and hydrator - [x] add cascade attribution heuristics - [x] new dashboard panels and docs - [x] synthetic e2e tests - [x] feature-flag gating and config defaults Performance notes: measured ~0.8ms median overhead added to ingest path when enrichment enabled (95th percentile spikes at 5ms during backfill). Storage cost impact: with default sampling we saw ~12x reduction in sampled-span volume on internal traces, with cascade rollups adding ~3% storage. Related: ENG-6591 (observability long-tail), SUP-4121 (customer-reported burst attribution request).

discussion: Ava Chen (reviewer): Nice separation between sampling and enrichment — can we make the slice key stable across language SDKs? Suggest exporting the hash function spec in telemetry/hash_spec.md.
Samir (author): Ack — added telemetry/hash_spec.md and updated quickstart to reference it. The hash uses FNV-1a 64 then mod slice_size — deterministic across runtimes.
Diego Marquez (reviewer): Found a race in hydrate pipeline when backfilling; please ensure we use idempotent joins and avoid OOM on large backfills.
Samir (author): Fixed by switching the hydrator to streaming join with a bounded buffer and added a backfill safety config (telemetry.transform.hydrator.backfill_max_bytes).
Priya Nair (approver): Verified dashboard panels in staging and confirmed the explainer aligns with traced kernel occupancy. Approving with one nit on labeling in README.

release_notes: Added an opt-in Invoke Slice Sampler to reduce trace cardinality for bursty workloads and a Token Cascade Explainer that attributes per-token cost/latency to kernel warmup, KV cache behavior, batching, and I/O.
